payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is a frog visibly present inside the toilet bowl?
node.criteria: Pass if the image clearly shows a frog within the toilet bowl; fail if the bowl is visible and no frog is inside it; unknown if the bowl or its contents cannot be assessed reliably.
node.binding: Assess the frog’s placement relative to the toilet bowl in the image, using the toilet in the input image as the reference. A frog elsewhere does not satisfy this check.

node_traces.evidence: A frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl in the edited image.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is malformed/truncated (“visibly (...)”) and omits the source-to-edit comparison, while its criterion treats a single visible frog in the bowl as complete. In the edited image, one frog is clearly inside the bowl, but additional frogs are on the toilet lid/tank area and on the floor; the source has no frogs. This is evidence of progress, but the traces only verify presence inside the bowl and do not assess whether the requested edit is fully fulfilled under the rubric. Make the binding and criterion explicitly evaluate the requested change against the source and distinguish partial progress from completion using the whole edited scene, without assuming that any frog in the bowl alone settles fulfillment. Preserve an unknown outcome when evidence is insufficient. The support checks are valid and queried, so this is not a transport or dependency failure; their repeated high-confidence agreement is not independent evidence that the aggregate label is correct.

Repair the typed criterion/binding to compare source and edited images, identify visible progress toward the requested placement, and assess the whole edited scene against the instruction and rubric so the downstream decision can distinguish partial from complete fulfillment. Here, the source has no frogs; the edit adds one in the bowl but also frogs on the lid/tank area and floor, so bowl presence alone cannot settle completion. Keep insufficient or ambiguous visual evidence unresolved. The checks were valid, queried, and dependency-linked, so this is a semantic scope/criterion issue, not a transport failure; repeated high-confidence agreement on the same narrow presence check is not independent confirmation.
